predicted: Section 11's open item, unchanged by R90: the safety argument rests on six harmful pools of which three are ACS variants, leaving MIMIC-IV and ACS TravelTime as the only independent evidence. R90 supplies the lever it also failed to use. Its scope condition is that carving -- and merging generally -- decides the marginal case, and BELOW the adequacy boundary there is no marginal case: at median EPV 3.04 every Freddie Mac carving helped ~63% of decisions regardless. So harm should be manufacturable on demand by capping a collection ABOVE the boundary rather than below it. These cap Freddie Mac and Lending Club to EPV ~25-40, far above the EPV-10 region, on partitions that helped everywhere at low adequacy. PREDICTION: mean benefit turns NEGATIVE on at least one of these, giving section 11 an independent harmful collection that is neither ACS nor clinical. FALSIFIABLE AND INFORMATIVE EITHER WAY: if every pool still helps at EPV 40, then harm is not a function of adequacy alone and section 4's gradient needs a stated scope condition of its own -- which would be a bigger finding than the harmful pool.
